newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Aznar sees Spain as Europe's bridge to LatAm.
newsitem.headline: Aznar sees Spain as Europe's bridge to LatAm.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said on Thursday that Spain wants to strengthen its role as Europe's bridge to Latin America and urged closer ties between both sides of the Atlantic.

Citing his country's deep cultural and historic links to the region, Aznar told a group of businessmen in Brazil's economic powerhouse of Sao Paulo that Madrid has made stronger ties between Europe and Ibero-America a cornerstone policy.
"Spain assumes as a political priority the strengthening of links between both shores of the Atlantic," he said on the first leg of a two-nation South American tour.
"We are determined to play this role of bridge between both worlds which history and our good will encourage us to develop," he added.
He said Spain would propose to fellow European Union (EU) members that the first summit between Ibero-American and EU heads of state be held in Latin America in 1999.

Aznar's trip is aimed at improving relations with Mercosur, one of the world's fastest-growing trade blocs. Brazil, the only major country in the region not colonised by Spain and where Portuguese is the official language, is the senior member of the four-nation customs union.

A staunch defender of the free market, Aznar urged the Brazilian government to push forward with economic reforms and the opening of the economy. Those efforts would result in steadily growing trade between Brazil and Europe, he said.

Last year, direct Spanish investment in Brazil reached $600 million and Brazil maintains a slight trade surplus with Spain, with exports of $937 million and imports totalling $902 million, according to Sao Paulo's Industry Federation (Fiesp).

"Spain's participation in Brazil's trade balance in general rose from 1.64 percent to 1.69 percent," Fiesp President Carlos Eduardo Moreira Ferreira told the group before Aznar's speech. "Although it is still small, it should increase."
Aznar arrived in Sao Paulo late on Wednesday and was slated to travel on Thursday to Brasilia.

He also will pay a visit to the southern state of Rio Grande do Sul, where Spain's Telefonica de Espana is an operating partner of a group that bought a controlling stake in Rio Grande do Sul's state-owned telecommunications firm CRT late last year.
After Brazil, he is to travel to Buenos Aires, where he will meet with Argentine officials, diplomatic sources said.
Aznar is the third EU head of state to visit Brazil in recent months.
